headline: QA-focused morning signal — agentic QA, serving gaps, test observability, and infra readiness

top_signal.title: How SWE-Serve exposes the gap between local tests and live serving
top_signal.summary: NVIDIA shows how changes that pass local unit and integration tests can still fail in real model-serving environments due to runtime differences, model loading, and request handling. The post analyzes real failure modes and investigation steps.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Signals a test-surface mismatch: teams must validate serving environments with end-to-end and canary tests, not just local unit suites.

items.title: Measuring the back/forward cache with Application Metrics
items.summary: Sentry released a bfcacheMetricsIntegration to surface back/forward cache hits/misses in application metrics, enabling detection of regressions invisible to standard page-load metrics.
items.why_it_matters: Makes bfcache behavior measurable in test and monitoring pipelines, helping QA detect navigation regressions and flaky user journeys earlier.

items.title: Professional skepticism is a dev’s best skill (flaky-test focus)
items.summary: Stack Overflow’s feature emphasizes professional skepticism in AI-driven development, discusses applying test-driven practices to agentic workflows, and highlights flaky-test root causes tied to application state.
items.why_it_matters: Reinforces people/process guidance: prioritize deterministic state, stronger test isolation, and skepticism when adopting agents that alter code or test flows.

items.title: Build your way: Use any AI agent of your choice in Android Studio
items.summary: Android Studio added Bring-Your-Own-Agent (BYOA) capability so teams can run custom coding agents or agentic tools inside the IDE, integrating third-party agents with Android’s tooling and workflows.
items.why_it_matters: Impacts mobile QA: agent-driven test generation or device orchestration can now run inside developers’ IDEs, changing how teams validate generated tests and agent actions.

items.title: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
items.category: Agentic QA safety / Test environment hygiene
items.summary: GitHub added local sandboxing controls to the Copilot app to limit file, network, and credential access during agent runs, reducing destructive side effects from generated commands.
items.why_it_matters: Improves safety for agentic QA: safer local execution reduces false failures from uncontrolled agent actions and makes unattended test-agent experiments less risky.

items.title: Validate GPU cluster readiness before AI workloads land
items.summary: NVIDIA published an active validation approach (NVCRE/AICR) showing how to run real multi-node GPU workloads and verification jobs to detect runtime configuration and networking issues that static checks miss.
items.why_it_matters: For QA owning AI infra, run active workload validations in CI or pre-production to catch runtime failures that unit checks and passive monitoring overlook.
